pages.lesson:
LESSON: WRITING 7.4.1 MECHANICS OF WRITING: PUNCTUATION

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 7
Topic 7.4: Writing 7.4.1 Mechanics of writing: Punctuation

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Writing 7.4.1 Mechanics of writing: Punctuation
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: Why do you use punctuation marks?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. identify commonly used punctuation marks in written texts for effective communication
2. use full stops and capital letters correctly in written texts for communication clarity

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Writing 7.4.1 Mechanics of writing: Punctuation

• Listen to a model.
• Study the example.
• Then produce your own example.

▸ Writing 7.4.1 Mechanics of writing: Punctuation

Teach
• Focus skill: identify commonly used punctuation marks in written texts for effective communication.
• Use complete sentences.
• Speak clearly; write neatly.

Worked example
• Model sentence 1 about Writing 7.4.1 Mechanics of writing: Punctuation.
• Model sentence 2 using a Kenyan school example.
• Model dialogue: A: “…?”  B: “…”

Try this
• Write 5 original sentences on this skill.
• Say one 30-second oral example to a partner.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• One clear model for Writing 7.4.1 Mechanics of writing: Punctuation
• One Kenyan school/home example

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences.
2. Do one oral practice with a partner.
3. Correct spelling/punctuation.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet: meaning + 5 examples + 5 practice items.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why do you use punctuation marks?
2. Which punctuation marks do you use when writing?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Model first, then try.
• Use complete sentences.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
